details.text: Use the email addresses or form on our contact page. Tell us about your research interests or what you would like to discuss. If you would like to visit, include your preferred timing.

studentsIntro: Design, implement, train, and evaluate your own models—and turn them into working systems. We welcome students who want to go beyond using existing AI.
skillsTitle: Four skills you will develop in the lab.

skills.label: DESIGN
skills.title: Build models
skills.description: Understand neural network architectures through small Transformers and latent diffusion models, then implement and improve them yourself.

skills.label: TRAIN
skills.title: Run training
skills.description: Use computing resources suited to your research and gain experience with automated data synthesis and distributed training. Develop the practical skills to see a research project through, from planning and experiments to evaluation and presenting results.

skills.label: EVALUATE
skills.title: Evaluate from multiple perspectives
skills.description: Assess not only accuracy, but also model size, response time, reproducibility, and usability to understand the value of an AI system.

skills.label: COLLABORATE
skills.title: Achieve results together
skills.description: Discuss ideas with faculty, students, and researchers at other institutions. Bring different perspectives together to move research forward.

fitTitle: For people who enjoy trial and error.
fitIntro: We value persistence, independent thinking, initiative, and curiosity more than innate talent.
fit: You investigate unfamiliar mathematics or code, experiment, and deepen your understanding step by step.
You want to understand why AI works and how to build it, engaging with the subject as a field of study.
You want to create across fields such as games, image generation, creativity support, and optimization.
You enjoy discussing ideas and making progress with others, as well as working independently.
requiredTitle: What we expect before you join

required.title: Basic Python skills
required.description: Be able to write simple programs using variables, conditionals, functions, lists, and dictionaries. You do not need to have mastered Python before joining.

required.title: Persistence in solving problems
required.description: Be willing to investigate errors and failures, isolate their causes, and keep moving forward.

required.title: Clear expression and careful understanding
required.description: We place a strong emphasis on articulating your ideas precisely and fully, while accurately understanding what others mean.

notRequiredTitle: What you can learn after joining
notRequired: How to use computing resources for distributed training
How to present at international conferences and write papers
The mathematical knowledge and expertise needed for your research
The skills to implement games and generative AI models
notRequiredNote: You do not need to have acquired this knowledge or these skills before joining. With curiosity and persistence, you will develop them gradually through research.

life.title: From small-scale replication studies to your own research questions
life.description: Begin by reproducing experiments and reading existing implementations, then develop your own problem statements and improvements. Visits to research collaborators also bring knowledge from real-world practice into your work.

life.title: Let questions start the conversation
life.description: Seminars include progress updates, technical discussions, design reviews, paper discussions, and interpretation of experimental results. Where appropriate, the work extends to partner discussions, external presentations, and demonstrations.

roadmapIntro: A guide to the fourth year. The pace and activities depend on your research topic and progress.

roadmap.label: FOUNDATIONS
roadmap.title: Build your foundations
roadmap.description: Set up your environment, learn Python and PyTorch fundamentals, read prior work, and study existing implementations. Reproduce experiments and make small improvements until you can run your own investigations.

roadmap.label: EXPLORATION
roadmap.title: Shape your own question
roadmap.description: Narrow your topic and plan experiments. Design models, datasets, and evaluation criteria, iterating until your ideas take shape as a research project.

roadmap.label: COMMUNICATION
roadmap.title: Bring your findings together
roadmap.description: Analyze your results and complete your undergraduate research project. Depending on the work, explore demonstrations, external presentations, and paper submissions.

faqIntro: Answers to common concerns about joining the lab.

faq.question: Do I need to be good at mathematics?
faq.answer: You do not need to be an expert at the start. You will learn the mathematics your research requires by connecting it with implementation. What matters is a willingness to investigate and gradually understand unfamiliar ideas.

faq.question: I am worried about reading papers in English.
faq.answer: Most people find it demanding at first. Rather than aiming for perfect understanding immediately, begin with the important figures, equations, and experimental settings, and build your reading skills over time.

faq.question: I have used generative AI, but I have never built a generative AI model.
faq.answer: We welcome students at that stage, too. Starting with basic Python skills, you will gain experience designing, implementing, and training models. Our focus is helping you progress from an AI user to an AI developer.

faq.question: How do I know whether research is right for me?
faq.answer: You do not have to arrive thinking like an experienced researcher. By building small things, testing ideas, and gradually going deeper, you can discover topics and ways of working that suit you.
